National Laboratory of the Rockies | 19 Aviation, Marine and Freight Aviation, Marine and Freight Aviation Fuel Aviation Fuel • Sustainable Aviation Fuel (SAF) is produced from non-petroleum feedstocks. • Feedstocks for SAF include fats, greases, oils, food and yard waste from municipal solid waste, woody biomass, and other feedstocks. • SAF can be blended, with limits, with conventional jet fuel at levels ranging from 10% to 50%, depending on the feedstock and the production process. • SAF, once blended with Jet A, meets ASTM D1655 and is used in existing aircraft and infrastructure. • According to the International Civil Aviation Organization, over 360,000 commercial flights have used SAF at 46 airports. • There are 6 domestic SAF production facilities Source: Alternative Fuels Data Center, Sustainable Aviation Fuel, n.d. National Laboratory of the Rockies | 21 Marine Transportation Marine Transportation • Next-generation marine fuels, including liquefied natural gas, methanol, ethanol, and ammonia, can be used in addition to conventional marine fuels. • Maritime propulsion systems could use electrified powertrains instead of mechanical ones. • Electric-based powertrains can support long-term vessel operability as technologies evolve over a ship’s 30-year or longer service life. Through a pilot project with the North Carolina Department of Transportation and Tidelands EMC, NREL is analyzing key • Hybrid marine engines could reduce fuel opportunities and challenges for electrifying ferries.Photo consumption by combining conventional engines by North Carolina Department of Transportation with electric propulsion. • Enhancing energy efficiency by optimizing designs of vessel equipment, recovering waste heat, and auxiliary machinery. Source: Department of Energy, Maritime Innovation, n.d. National Laboratory of the Rockies | 22 Freight Rail Transport Freight Rail Transport • Moving freight by rail is the most fuel-efficient method to move freight over land and, by freight ton-mile, can be up to four times more efficient than truck transit. • The ALTRIOS tool can support railway operators, locomotive manufacturers, regulatory agencies, and other organizations explore optimized and cost-effective solutions for advanced and efficient rail technologies. Photo from NLR • The INFORMES tool supports advanced freight technologies for rail, marine, and trucking Source: National Laboratory of the Rockies, n.d. National Laboratory of the Rockies | 23 Public Transit Public Transit Public Transit Public Transit • Public transportation options include: ◦ Ferries ◦ Rail ◦ Trolleys ◦ Buses. • Buses are well-suited for using alternative fuels. • High ridership can reduce vehicle miles traveled, fuel used for private vehicles and congestion. • Tools that support transit planning ◦ RoutE Compass is an energy-aware routing tool that incorporates energy consumption predictions Image from NLR into network routing algorithms. Capabilities include vehicle route optimization and selection, time and energy trade-offs evaluation and more. Source: Alternative Fuels
